newsitem.title: USA: US High Court allows natural gas pipeline order.
newsitem.headline: US High Court allows natural gas pipeline order.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Monday rejected challenges to a 1992 order by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commssion restructuring the natural gas pipeline business.

The justices, without comment or dissent, let stand a U.S. appeals court ruling in July that upheld in large part FERC's Order No. 636 designed to improve the competitive structure of the natural gas industry.
The order mandated the "unbundling" of interstate natural gas service from transportation service, requiring that those services be sold separately to natural gas purchasers.

The appeals court concluded that FERC's jurisdiction over interstate transportation of gas on interstate pipelines gives it the authority to regulate the exchange of interstate transportation capacity.
The order imposed "capacity-release" requirements that allow holders of firm transportation rights on interstate pipelines to resell those rights under uniform terms.

The court rejected several challenges to FERC's rules giving a pipeline customer the right of first refusal for a new contract for capacity when its existing term expires if it can match the best offer the pipeline gets from other bidders.

The appeals court said FERC included adequate safeguards against pipeline manipulation of bids and found no basis to require that pipelines accept bids at less than the approved rates. It said FERC provided proper incentives to encourage pipelines to accept discounted bids.

High court appeals were filed in four cases. Among those opposing the rules were the Associated Gas Distributors, a trade group of local natural gas distribution utilities, the American Public Gas Association, a trade group of local distribution systems, and state regulators.
But the Supreme Court sided with FERC, denying the appeals and refusing to review the case.
